question:
A figure skater performs a spin as part of their routine.

Explain Newton's Laws of Motion in relation to the skater spinning and how the skater can alter their rate of spin.

(AO1 = 4 marks, AO2 = 5 marks, AO3 = 6 marks)
markScheme:
Indicative content — mark holistically using the levels below.
AO1: Newton's First Law (of rotation) states a body will continue to turn about its axis of rotation with constant angular momentum unless an external force is exerted upon it.
AO2: applying this to the skater — the skater will continue to spin with constant angular momentum unless an external force acts on them (e.g. friction with the ice).
AO3: this is the principle of conservation of angular momentum; angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular velocity; the skater can alter their rate of spin by moving their limbs closer to or further from the axis of rotation — bringing arms/legs close to the body decreases moment of inertia, increasing angular velocity (speeding up the spin); extending limbs outward increases moment of inertia, decreasing angular velocity (slowing the spin); if the skater has not warmed up appropriately, they may be unable to achieve the optimal tucked position, reducing spin efficiency, and reduced oxygen delivery could cause earlier fatigue, reducing control of the spin.
Band 5 (13-15): Comprehensive, accurate, well-linked discussion across all AOs.
Band 4 (10-12): Good detail and mostly accurate application/discussion, minor omissions.
Band 3 (7-9): Reasonable but partial coverage, some analysis attempted.
Band 2 (4-6): Basic knowledge, limited application/discussion.
Band 1 (1-3): Fragmented, largely irrelevant or highly limited.
0 marks: No relevant content.
Max 15 marks.

question: Trampolinists have to change the position of their body when performing a somersault. Explain how a trampolinist alters their angular velocity by changing their moment of inertia.
markScheme:
4 marks from:
- Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular velocity; angular momentum remains constant during flight/rotation (conservation of angular momentum).
- To slow down the rotation, the trampolinist increases their moment of inertia.
- This is achieved by extending the body/opening out.
- To increase the speed of rotation, the trampolinist decreases their moment of inertia, achieved by tucking the body/bringing the limbs towards the axis of rotation.
Max 4 marks.

question: Explain how a diver can alter the speed of rotation during flight in relation to angular motion.
markScheme:
Indicative content — mark using levels of response.
- Changing the shape of the body causes a change in speed of rotation.
- A change in moment of inertia leads to a change in angular velocity/speed of rotation/angular momentum.
- Angular momentum remains constant during flight/rotation; angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular velocity.
- Angular momentum is the quantity of rotation/motion; angular velocity is the speed of rotation; moment of inertia is the spread/distribution of mass around an axis/the body's reluctance to rotate.
- To slow down rotation, the diver increases their moment of inertia, achieved by extending the body/opening out (e.g. straightening from a tuck into a pike or layout before entry).
- To increase the speed of rotation, the diver decreases their moment of inertia, achieved by tucking the body/bringing limbs closer to the axis of rotation.
Max 8 marks.
